paragraphs.text: No. The filing representative cannot attest for the applicant or owner and cannot submit this job filing. The Applicant of Record must complete the applicant attestation and electronic signature before submission; the applicant also must review the filing, provide the final electronic signature, and officially submit it electronically. Filing representatives may enter and view filing information, but they cannot submit filings or permits.

The owner must review the filing and personally complete the Owner’s Attestation in the Statements & Signatures tab, using the same email address entered for the owner in the Stakeholders section. All DOB NOW job filings require the owner’s confirmation authorizing the applicant to submit and acknowledging review of the application. The representative can use Preview to File to identify what remains incomplete before the applicant submits.

If the filing’s Owner Type is Condo Unit Owner or Co-Op Tenant-Shareholder, the Board representative is also a required stakeholder and must log in and attest; both the owner and Board representative must complete their attestations before the filing can proceed. The facts provided do not identify the Owner Type, so this additional condition may apply.

paragraphs.text: The plumbing scope should be filed as a subsequent filing under the existing job number, not as a new unrelated job number, if it is part of the same construction project and property. The guidance says all filings for the same construction project should use the same job number with an alphabetic/numeric filing extension; a subsequent filing adds new scope of work and new work types on the same property and may use a new applicant. Although it is strongly encouraged rather than framed here as an absolute prohibition on a separate job, the stated workflow preference is to use the subsequent filing.

Because the initial GC filing has already been created, the guidance supports locating that initial (I1) filing—by BIN search or known job-number search—and selecting the Subsequent Filing action. The subsequent plumbing application functions as a separate application, may have a different review type, and can be permitted before the initial filing is permitted. It may be initiated and submitted after the I1 has been submitted and before an LOC is issued for the I1; the supplied facts do not say whether the I1 has been submitted, so that submission-status prerequisite remains to be confirmed.

The supplied FAQ also says a subsequent filing created while the I1 remains in pre-filing status may have I1-populated fields grayed out and recommends completing as much of the I1 as possible before creating the subsequent filing; it does not clearly establish that creation is categorically unavailable before I1 submission. For the stated plan to file plumbing later, however, submission of the subsequent application is expressly tied to the I1 having been submitted.

missingFacts: Whether the existing initial GC filing has been submitted (rather than remaining in pre-filing status), which affects readiness to submit the subsequent plumbing filing.
evidenceLimitations: The supplied guidance does not state a plumbing-specific exception to the same-project/same-property subsequent-filing workflow.

The supplied FAQ gives an express timing rule for initiating and submitting a subsequent filing after I1 submission, while separately describing a subsequent filing in pre-filing status; it leaves the precise availability and effect of creation before I1 submission unresolved.
